newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Feb 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Feb 14.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Friday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* The Dow industrials closed above 7,000 for the first time, surging 60.81 to 7,022.44. The S&P also set a record, rising 9.05 to 811.82.
* Contract talks between AMR's American Airlines and the pilots' union stalled, and the White House is considering stepping in to ward off a strike.
* Retail sales rose 0.6 percent in January, above December's 0.3 gain.
* ITT Corp agreed to sell three million shares in French telecommunications company Alcatel-Alsthom for $301 million to try to thwart Hilton Hotels' hostile bid.
* Campbell Soup settled its dispute with H.J. Heinz over a Campbell executive Heinz hired.
* Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan said he supports an overhaul of the nation's banking laws but is against giving federal deposit insurance to securities, insurance and other industries.
* Talisman Energy said it will make a cash-and-stock offer valued at $1.15 billion for Canada's Wascana Energy.
* General Motors may have to close some of its truck plants if supplier American Axle & Manufacturing is unable to avoid a strike scheduled to begin Friday night.
* Philips Electronics posted heavy losses for the fourth quarter and the year amid management resignations and an uncertain long-term strategy.
* The Justice Department has extended for another month its antitrust review of Raytheon's proposed acquisition of Texas Instruments defense business.
* U.S. satellite companies won a victory after the Intelsat satellite consortium agreed to delay its effort to privatize part of the system.
* Britain's Pearson said it will take a pretax charge of $163.1 million because of accounting irregularities at its Penguin USA book publishing unit.
* The Federal Reserve Board fined Asahi Bank of Japan $5 million for allegedly allowing some bank employees to illegally examine confidential Fed documents.
* Musicland said it reached a pact with its suppliers to defer payment on millions of dollars it owes them.
* They laughed when Ralph Acampora forecast Dow 7000 back in June 1995, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average just above 4000.

Now, despite what many see as high valuations in stock prices, it is Mr Acampora, chief technical analyst at Prudential Securities Inc, who is laughing -- and forecasting Dow 8250 before year's end. -- Heard on the Street.
* Two record-breaking issues of emerging-markets bonds left investors applauding this week, but some analysts are scratching their heads. -- Credit Markets.
